source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: verse numbers follow the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: This chapter is numbered as in the Hebrew text. Hebrew 5:20-26 are numbered 6:1-7 in many Bibles, so Hebrew 6:1-23, the verses of this chapter, are 6:8-30 there, and the Hebrew chapter 7 begins at the same point in both. Leviticus is cited here by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: a new speech: instructions for the priests
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-5 told the people what to bring. From here to 7:38 the same offerings are taken up again, now with the rules the priests must follow for each (6:2, 7, 18; 7:1, 11).

source.text: צַ֤ו אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הָעֹלָ֑ה הִ֣וא הָעֹלָ֡ה עַל֩ מוֹקְדָ֨ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֤חַ כָּל־הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר וְאֵ֥שׁ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ תּ֥וּקַד בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Command Aaron and his sons, saying, this [is the] law of the burnt offering: it [is] the burnt offering on [the] hearth on the altar all the night until the morning, and [the] fire of the altar will burn on it.

en.L: "Command Aaron and his sons, saying, 'This [is] the law of the burnt offering: it, the burnt offering, [shall be] on the hearth on the altar all the night until the morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
en.B: "Give Aaron and his sons this command: 'These are the instructions for the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to stay on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the altar fire must be kept burning on it.
en.R: "Give Aaron and his sons this order: 'Here are the rules for the burnt offering. The burnt offering must stay on the fire on the altar all night long, until morning. The fire on the altar must keep burning.

decisions.choice: law: instruction, the set procedure for a rite
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction. In 6:2-7:37 it names the rules for one kind of offering, the way it is to be done, and each section opens with "This is the law of ..." (6:7, 18; 7:1, 11). The same pattern is used for the rules on uncleanness in chapters 11-15 (11:46; 12:7; 13:59).

decisions.choice: command: a stronger word than "speak"
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-5 opened "Speak to the sons of Israel"; this speech is a command to the priests, who are responsible for carrying it out.

decisions.choice: hearth: the place on the altar where the fire burns
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb for burning and occurs only here. The burnt offering of the evening (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8) was to burn through the night on the altar fire.

decisions.choice: instructions / rules
decisions.reason: Balanced says "instructions" and Readable "rules" for this sense of the word. Literal keeps "law".

decisions.choice: this command / this order
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the words to be passed on; Balanced and Readable fold it into "give ... this command".

source.text: וְלָבַ֨שׁ הַכֹּהֵ֜ן מִדּ֣וֹ בַ֗ד וּמִֽכְנְסֵי־בַד֮ יִלְבַּ֣שׁ עַל־בְּשָׂרוֹ֒ וְהֵרִ֣ים אֶת־הַדֶּ֗שֶׁן אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאכַ֥ל הָאֵ֛שׁ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֖ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְשָׂמ֕וֹ אֵ֖צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will put on the priest his garment of linen, and undergarments of linen he will put on over his flesh, and he will lift up the fatty ash which consumes the fire, the burnt offering, on the altar, and he will place it beside the altar.

en.L: And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and linen undergarments he shall put on over his flesh, and he shall lift up the fatty ashes [to] which the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
en.B: The priest is to put on his linen robe, with linen undergarments next to his body. Then he is to take up the ashes left when the fire has burned up the burnt offering on the altar, and put them beside the altar.
en.R: The priest must put on his linen robe and his linen underwear. Then he must take away the ashes left from the burnt offering that the fire burned up on the altar. He must put them beside the altar.

decisions.choice: the fatty ashes: the ash of wood mixed with the fat of the offerings
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "fat". It names what is left on the altar when the fire has burned the offerings and their fat: an oily ash. The same word is used of the ash heap east of the altar in 1:16 and of the place outside the camp in 4:12. It is not common rubbish: it is first set beside the altar and then carried to a clean place (verse 4).

decisions.choice: linen garment and undergarments: the priest's clothing for the altar
decisions.reason: Linen clothing for the priests is described in Exodus 28:39-43, where the linen undergarments are to cover the body "from the waist to the thighs" so that the priest is not exposed at the altar. The garment here may be the priest's tunic. Even taking away ashes is holy work and is done in holy clothing.

decisions.choice: which the fire consumes, the burnt offering: the ashes of the burnt offering after the fire has burned it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the ashes "which the fire consumes the burnt offering". The sense is the ash that is left when the fire has burned up the burnt offering.

decisions.choice: the ashes
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fatty ashes", which shows the root; Balanced and Readable say "ashes" (1:16).

source.text: וּפָשַׁט֙ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְלָבַ֖שׁ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְהוֹצִ֤יא אֶת־הַדֶּ֨שֶׁן֙ אֶל־מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אֶל־מָק֖וֹם טָהֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will strip off his garments and put on other garments, and he will bring out the fatty ash to outside the camp, to a place clean.

en.L: And he shall take off his garments and put on other garments, and he shall bring out the fatty ashes to outside the camp, to a clean place.
en.B: Then he is to take off these clothes, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes out of the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
en.R: Then he must change into other clothes and carry the ashes outside the camp. He must take them to a place that is clean.

decisions.choice: other garments: ordinary clothing for work outside the holy area
decisions.reason: The holy linen clothing belongs at the altar. To go out of the camp the priest changes into other clothes, keeping what is holy apart from what is common (compare 16:23-24 and Ezekiel 44:19).

decisions.choice: a clean place: a place fit for holy remains, as in 4:12
decisions.reason: The ashes of the offerings are not thrown just anywhere. They go to a place outside the camp that is ritually clean, the same place to which the remains of a sin offering are taken (4:12).

source.text: וְהָאֵ֨שׁ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֤חַ תּֽוּקַד־בּוֹ֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה וּבִעֵ֨ר עָלֶ֧יהָ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן עֵצִ֖ים בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וְעָרַ֤ךְ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ הָֽעֹלָ֔ה וְהִקְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ חֶלְבֵ֥י הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And the fire on the altar will burn on it; not will it be quenched, and will kindle on it the priest wood in the morning, in the morning, and he will arrange on it the burnt offering and make smoke on it [the] fats of the peace offerings.

en.L: And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. And the priest shall kindle wood on it morning by morning, and he shall arrange the burnt offering on it and make the fat portions of the peace offerings smoke on it.
en.B: The fire on the altar must be kept burning and must not go out. Every morning the priest is to put more wood on it, lay out the burnt offering on it, and burn on it the fat from the peace offerings.
en.R: The fire on the altar must keep burning. It must not go out. Every morning the priest must add wood to the fire. He must place the burnt offering on it and burn the fat of the peace offerings there.

decisions.choice: in the morning, in the morning: every morning
decisions.reason: Repeating the phrase makes it distributive: each morning, day after day.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering and the fat of the peace offerings: the daily offerings burned on the morning fire
decisions.reason: The morning burnt offering (Exodus 29:38-39) was laid on the fresh wood, and the fat of any peace offerings brought that day was burned on top of it, as 3:5 says.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn on the altar, so that it goes up as smoke
decisions.reason: The verb used for burning offerings on the altar means to turn them into smoke that rises to God (1:9). It is a different verb from the one for burning refuse outside the camp (verse 23).

source.text: אֵ֗שׁ תָּמִ֛יד תּוּקַ֥ד עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לֹ֥א תִכְבֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A fire continually will burn on the altar; not will it be quenched.

en.L: A fire shall burn continually on the altar; it shall not go out.
en.B: Fire is to burn on the altar at all times, never going out.
en.R: There must always be a fire burning on the altar. No one may let it die out.

decisions.choice: a fire continually: an altar fire that never goes out
decisions.reason: The fire first came from the LORD himself when the altar was dedicated (9:24). Keeping it always burning kept the offerings going up day and night, and it is stated twice (verses 5 and 6) for emphasis.

decisions.choice: No one may let it die out
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that this is a duty laid on the priests.

source.text: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַקְרֵ֨ב אֹתָ֤הּ בְּנֵֽי־אַהֲרֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֖י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is the] law of the grain offering: present it [the] sons of Aaron before Yahweh, to [the] front of the altar.

en.L: And this [is] the law of the grain offering: the sons of Aaron shall bring it near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the front of the altar.
en.B: These are the instructions for the grain offering. Aaron's sons are to present it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of the altar.
en.R: Here are the rules for the grain offering. Aaron's sons must bring it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of the altar.

decisions.choice: the grain offering: the offering of 2:1-16, now from the priests' side
decisions.reason: The kinds of grain offering are described in chapter 2 (see 2:1). These verses tell the priests what to do with the portion burned and the part they eat.

decisions.choice: to the front of the altar: the west side, facing the tent
decisions.reason: The side of the altar that faces the tent of meeting, where offerings were set down before the priest took a handful to burn (2:8).

source.text: וְהֵרִ֨ים מִמֶּ֜נּוּ בְּקֻמְצ֗וֹ מִסֹּ֤לֶת הַמִּנְחָה֙ וּמִשַּׁמְנָ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־הַלְּבֹנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ רֵ֧יחַ נִיחֹ֛חַ אַזְכָּרָתָ֖הּ לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will lift up from it in his handful from [the] fine flour of the grain offering and from its oil, and all the frankincense which [is] on the grain offering, and he will make smoke the altar, an aroma of soothing, its memorial portion to Yahweh.

en.L: And he shall lift from it in his handful some of the fine flour of the grain offering and some of its oil, and all the frankincense that [is] on the grain offering, and make [it] smoke [on] the altar, an aroma of soothing, its memorial portion to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The priest is to take up a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering with some of its oil, along with all the frankincense on it, and burn it on the altar as its memorial portion, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The priest must take a handful of the fine flour with some of its oil. He must also take all the frankincense on the grain offering. He must burn this on the altar. It is the part that is a reminder, a smell that pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: his handful ... its memorial portion: as in 2:2
decisions.reason: The handful burned on the altar stands for the whole offering and is called its memorial portion (2:2). The rest goes to the priests (verse 9).

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: an offering that pleases God, as in 1:9
decisions.reason: The phrase describes the smoke of an offering that God accepts with pleasure (1:9).

decisions.choice: The priest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he"; one of Aaron's sons (verse 7) does this. Balanced and Readable name him as "the priest".

source.text: וְהַנּוֹתֶ֣רֶת מִמֶּ֔נָּה יֹאכְל֖וּ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּבָנָ֑יו מַצּ֤וֹת תֵּֽאָכֵל֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם קָדֹ֔שׁ בַּחֲצַ֥ר אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֖ד יֹאכְלֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the remainder of it will eat Aaron and his sons; unleavened it will be eaten in a place holy; in [the] courtyard of [the] tent of meeting they will eat it.

en.L: And the remainder of it Aaron and his sons shall eat; [as] unleavened [bread] it shall be eaten, in a holy place; in the courtyard of the tent of meeting they shall eat it.
en.B: What is left of it belongs to Aaron and his sons as food. They must eat it as bread made without yeast, and in a holy place: the courtyard of the tent of meeting is where they must eat it.
en.R: Aaron and his sons may eat what is left. They must eat it as bread made without yeast. They must eat it in a holy place, in the courtyard of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: unleavened it shall be eaten: eaten as unleavened bread
decisions.reason: The priests' share is to be baked and eaten without leaven, like the offering itself (2:4, 11; verse 10).

decisions.choice: a holy place, the courtyard of the tent of meeting: within the holy area
decisions.reason: Because the offering is most holy (verse 10), it may not be taken home. It is eaten inside the courtyard around the tent, where only those who are holy may go.

source.text: לֹ֤א תֵאָפֶה֙ חָמֵ֔ץ חֶלְקָ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֹתָ֖הּ מֵאִשָּׁ֑י קֹ֤דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁים֙ הִ֔וא כַּחַטָּ֖את וְכָאָשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will it be baked leavened; [as] their share I have given it from my fire offerings; a holy of holy things it [is], like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.

en.L: It shall not be baked leavened. [As] their share I have given it from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offerings by fire. It [is] a most holy [thing], like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.
en.B: It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
en.R: It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to the priests as their share of the food offerings burned for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. It is very holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.

decisions.choice: their share I have given: the priests' food is God's gift from what is his
decisions.reason: The offerings belong to God. He gives a share of them to the priests, who have no land of their own to farm (Numbers 18:8-20). Their food comes from his table.

decisions.choice: a holy of holy things: most holy, as in 2:3
decisions.reason: Most holy offerings may be eaten only by the priests, and only in the holy place (verses 9 and 11).

decisions.choice: like the sin offering and like the guilt offering
decisions.reason: The rules for those offerings follow in 6:17-23 and 7:1-7. All three are most holy and eaten by the priests in the same way.

decisions.choice: to the priests
decisions.reason: Readable names the priests as "them".

source.text: כָּל־זָכָ֞ר בִּבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ יֹֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה חָק־עוֹלָם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵאִשֵּׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּ֥ע בָּהֶ֖ם יִקְדָּֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Every male among [the] sons of Aaron will eat it, a portion forever for your generations from [the] fire offerings of Yahweh; all who touch them will become holy.

en.L: Every male among the sons of Aaron shall eat it, a portion forever for your generations from the offerings by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Whoever touches them will become holy.'"
en.B: Any male descendant of Aaron may eat it. It is their permanent share of the food offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for all your generations. Whoever touches these offerings will become holy.'"
en.R: Any male in Aaron's family may eat it. This will always be their share of the food offerings burned for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for all time to come. Anyone who touches these offerings will become holy.'"

decisions.choice: a portion forever: a lasting share, not a statute
decisions.reason: The word here means a fixed portion or allowance. Joined to "forever" it names a share that is always to be theirs. A related word for a statute appears in 3:17; this is the priests' due.

decisions.choice: every male among the sons of Aaron: men of the priestly family
decisions.reason: Any male of Aaron's line may eat it, not only the priest on duty, so long as he is clean (compare 21:22). The women of the priests' households share only the less holy portions (10:14; 22:12-13).

decisions.choice: whoever touches them will become holy: holiness passes by touch
alternatives: whoever touches them must be holy
whatever touches them will become holy
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "will become holy" or "must be holy". Most holy things pass on their holiness, so that whoever touches them comes to belong to God's holy sphere and is bound by its rules (Exodus 29:37; 30:29). The phrase may also mean that only those already holy may touch them. The Hebrew can mean "whatever touches them" as well as "whoever".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech: the priests' own grain offering
decisions.reason: These verses (13-16) break into the instructions to deal with the grain offering the priests bring for themselves, which is not eaten.

source.text: זֶ֡ה קָרְבַּן֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן וּבָנָ֜יו אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִ֣יבוּ לַֽיהוָ֗ה בְּיוֹם֙ הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֔וֹ עֲשִׂירִ֨ת הָאֵפָ֥ה סֹ֛לֶת מִנְחָ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד מַחֲצִיתָ֣הּ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וּמַחֲצִיתָ֖הּ בָּעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] offering of Aaron and his sons which they will present to Yahweh on [the] day [when] he is anointed: a tenth of the ephah [of] fine flour, a grain offering continually, its half in the morning and its half in the evening.

en.L: "This [is] the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall bring near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour [as] a grain offering continually, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
en.B: "This is the offering that Aaron and his sons are to present to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the day he is anointed: {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
en.R: "Here is the offering that Aaron and his sons must bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the day he is anointed. They must bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour as a grain offering every day. Half of it must be offered in the morning and half in the evening.

decisions.choice: on the day he is anointed: from that day on
alternatives: an offering on the day of anointing only
decisions.reason: "He" is the high priest, Aaron at first and then each son anointed after him (verse 15). The offering begins on the day of anointing and continues "continually", day by day. Some take the verse to mean an offering made by each priest on the day of his own anointing (compare 8:26-28), but "continually" and "morning and evening" point to a daily offering.

decisions.choice: a tenth of an ephah: about two quarts of flour, as in 5:11
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure of grain; a tenth of it is the amount brought by the poorest worshiper in 5:11 and offered with each daily lamb (Exodus 29:40).

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, every day
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the burnt offering offered every morning and evening (Exodus 29:42) and of the fire that never goes out (verse 6).

decisions.choice: from the day
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "from" the day, which makes plain that the offering begins then and continues (see m1).

source.text: עַֽל־מַחֲבַ֗ת בַּשֶּׁ֛מֶן תֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה מֻרְבֶּ֣כֶת תְּבִיאֶ֑נָּה תֻּפִינֵי֙ מִנְחַ֣ת פִּתִּ֔ים תַּקְרִ֥יב רֵֽיחַ־נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: On a griddle with oil it will be made; well mixed you will bring it; baked pieces of a grain offering of crumbs you will present, an aroma of soothing to Yahweh.

en.L: On a griddle with oil it shall be made; well soaked you shall bring it in; [as] baked pieces of a grain offering of broken bits you shall bring it near, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: It is to be made with oil on a griddle. Bring it in well soaked, and present it as a grain offering broken into pieces, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: It must be made with oil on a flat pan. Bring it when it is soaked through with oil. Break it into pieces and offer it as a grain offering. It is a smell that pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: well soaked: mixed thoroughly with oil
decisions.reason: The word is used only here, in 7:12 and in 1 Chronicles 23:29, always of flour and oil. It means flour that is soaked through, or dough well mixed, with oil.

decisions.choice: baked pieces: a word whose exact sense is unknown
decisions.reason: This word occurs nowhere else. From the context and the word "crumbs" or "broken bits" beside it, it seems to describe the cake baked and then broken in pieces, as with the griddle offering of 2:6. Others connect it with a word for baking, "baked" or "cooked".

decisions.choice: you will bring ... you will present: a word to the priest
decisions.reason: The speech turns to address the priest directly, as it does in 6:20 and 7:32.

decisions.choice: a flat pan
decisions.reason: Readable says "flat pan" for the griddle, a flat iron plate for baking (2:5).

source.text: וְהַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַמָּשִׁ֧יחַ תַּחְתָּ֛יו מִבָּנָ֖יו יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ חָק־עוֹלָ֕ם לַיהוָ֖ה כָּלִ֥יל תָּקְטָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priest the anointed in his place from his sons will make it; a portion forever to Yahweh; wholly it will be made to smoke.

en.L: And the anointed priest who [is] in his place from among his sons shall make it, a portion forever to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it shall be made to smoke whole.
en.B: The son who succeeds him as the anointed priest is to prepare it. This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s permanent due: it must be burned completely.
en.R: Each of Aaron's sons who becomes the high priest after him must offer it. It is always to be given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All of it must be burned up.

decisions.choice: the anointed priest: the high priest
decisions.reason: The "anointed priest" is the high priest, as in 4:3. This offering passes from Aaron to the son who takes his place in each generation.

decisions.choice: a portion forever to Yahweh: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The phrase used of the priests' share in verse 11 is used here of what is due to the LORD: this offering is his entirely.

decisions.choice: wholly: as a whole offering, nothing left
decisions.reason: The word means "whole" or "complete"; it is used for an offering burned entirely (Deuteronomy 33:10; 1 Samuel 7:9).

decisions.choice: the high priest
decisions.reason: Readable names the anointed priest by his usual title.

source.text: וְכָל־מִנְחַ֥ת כֹּהֵ֛ן כָּלִ֥יל תִּהְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵאָכֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And every grain offering of a priest whole will be; not will it be eaten.

en.L: And every grain offering of a priest shall be whole; it shall not be eaten."
en.B: Every grain offering a priest brings for himself is to be burned whole; it must not be eaten."
en.R: Any grain offering that a priest brings for himself must be burned up completely. No one may eat it."

decisions.choice: a priest's grain offering is not eaten
decisions.reason: When others bring a grain offering, the priest eats most of it (verse 9). He may not eat from his own offering: if he did, he would be giving nothing. So all of it goes to God.

decisions.choice: brings for himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that this is an offering the priest brings on his own behalf.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech, running on to 7:21
decisions.reason: This speech has no close before 7:21; the next new speech begins at 7:22. The instructions for the sin offering and guilt offering, and for the peace offering, belong to it.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַֽחַטָּ֑את בִּמְק֡וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ תִּשָּׁחֵ֨ט הָעֹלָ֜ה תִּשָּׁחֵ֤ט הַֽחַטָּאת֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, this [is the] law of the sin offering: in [the] place where is slaughtered the burnt offering will be slaughtered the sin offering before Yahweh; a holy of holy things it [is].

en.L: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, 'This [is] the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: "Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: 'These are the instructions for the sin offering. The sin offering is to be slaughtered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the same place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
en.R: "Tell Aaron and his sons: 'Here are the rules for the sin offering. Kill the animal for the sin offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, at the place where the animals for burnt offerings are killed. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: the sin offering: the purification offering of chapter 4, as in 4:3
decisions.reason: The rules for bringing it were given in 4:1-5:13. Here the priests learn where it is killed, who eats it, and how to deal with what touches it.

decisions.choice: the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered: north of the altar
decisions.reason: That place is "on the north side of the altar" (1:11). The sin offering is killed in the same holy place.

decisions.choice: most holy: as in verse 10
decisions.reason: Like the grain offering, the sin offering may be eaten only by the priests, in the holy place (verses 19 and 22).

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: Readable says "kill" for the word for slaughtering an animal for sacrifice.

source.text: הַכֹּהֵ֛ן הַֽמְחַטֵּ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ יֹאכֲלֶ֑נָּה בְּמָק֤וֹם קָדֹשׁ֙ תֵּֽאָכֵ֔ל בַּחֲצַ֖ר אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: The priest who offers it for sin will eat it; in a place holy it will be eaten, in [the] courtyard of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
en.B: The priest who offers it for sin is to eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
en.R: The priest who offers the sin offering must eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: who offers it for sin: who performs the purification rite with it
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for sin and means to cleanse from sin, to perform the sin offering. The priest who does so receives the meat (compare 10:17, where eating it is part of bearing the people's guilt).

decisions.choice: in a holy place: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The courtyard of the tent, as for the grain offering (verse 9).

source.text: כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּ֥ע בִּבְשָׂרָ֖הּ יִקְדָּ֑שׁ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִזֶּ֤ה מִדָּמָהּ֙ עַל־הַבֶּ֔גֶד אֲשֶׁר֙ יִזֶּ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ תְּכַבֵּ֖ס בְּמָק֥וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: All that touches its flesh will become holy, and [one] who spatters some of its blood on the garment, what he spatters on it you will wash in a place holy.

en.L: Everything that touches its flesh will become holy; and when some of its blood spatters on a garment, what it spattered on you shall wash in a holy place.
en.B: Whatever touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood spatters on a garment, you must wash the stained part in a holy place.
en.R: Anything that touches the meat will become holy. If any blood splashes on a piece of clothing, you must wash it in a holy place.

decisions.choice: everything that touches its flesh will become holy: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The meat is most holy, and what touches it shares that holiness. A garment stained with its blood must therefore be washed inside the holy area, not taken out of it. See the note on verse 11.

decisions.choice: spatters: falls by accident
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the priest's sprinkling of blood (4:6), but here it means drops that fall by accident, as the person who sprinkles would make them, on a garment.

decisions.choice: spatters / splashes
decisions.reason: Elsewhere this verb is "sprinkle", a deliberate act (4:6). Here it is an accident, so all levels say "spatter", and Readable "splash".

source.text: וּכְלִי־חֶ֛רֶשׂ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּבֻשַּׁל־בּ֖וֹ יִשָּׁבֵ֑ר וְאִם־בִּכְלִ֤י נְחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ בֻּשָּׁ֔לָה וּמֹרַ֥ק וְשֻׁטַּ֖ף בַּמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And a vessel of earthenware in which it is boiled will be broken; and if in a vessel of bronze it was boiled, then it will be scoured and rinsed with water.

en.L: And an earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
en.B: Any clay pot it is boiled in must be broken. If it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
en.R: If the meat is cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.

decisions.choice: earthenware ... bronze: clay soaks up what is cooked in it; metal can be cleaned
decisions.reason: Unglazed clay absorbs the juices of what is cooked in it, so a holy thing cannot be fully removed and the pot is broken. A metal pot can be scoured clean. The same rule applies to clay pots made unclean (11:33; 15:12).

source.text: כָּל־זָכָ֥ר בַּכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יֹאכַ֣ל אֹתָ֑הּ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: Every male among the priests will eat it; a holy of holy things it [is].

en.L: Every male among the priests shall eat it; it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: Any male of priestly descent may eat it. It is most holy.
en.R: Any male in the priests' families may eat it. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: every male among the priests: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: Verse 19 says the priest who offers it eats it. This verse adds that he may share it with the other males of the priestly families.

source.text: וְכָל־חַטָּ֡את אֲשֶׁר֩ יוּבָ֨א מִדָּמָ֜הּ אֶל־אֹ֧הֶל מוֹעֵ֛ד לְכַפֵּ֥ר בַּקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לֹ֣א תֵאָכֵ֑ל בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשָּׂרֵֽף׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And any sin offering which is brought some of its blood into [the] tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place, not will it be eaten; with fire it will be burned.

en.L: And any sin offering of which some of its blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire.
en.B: But no sin offering is to be eaten if any of its blood has been brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place. It must be burned in the fire.
en.R: But some sin offerings must not be eaten. If any of the animal's blood is brought inside the meeting tent to make atonement in the holy place, the meat must be burned up.

decisions.choice: blood brought into the tent of meeting: the sin offerings of 4:3-21
decisions.reason: For the sin of the anointed priest or of the whole community, blood was taken into the tent and sprinkled before the veil (4:5-7, 16-18). Those animals were burned outside the camp (4:11-12, 21). The priests may eat only the sin offerings whose blood is put on the altar outside (4:25, 30). Moses later rebukes Aaron's sons for not eating one of these (10:16-18).

decisions.choice: to make atonement: as in 1:4
decisions.reason: The blood is brought in to make atonement for the priest or for the whole community (4:3, 13).

decisions.choice: the holy place: the holy room of the tent
decisions.reason: Here "the holy" is the outer room of the tent, where the blood is sprinkled before the veil (4:6), not the inner room behind it.

decisions.choice: burned: destroyed by fire
decisions.reason: This is the ordinary verb for burning, not the verb used for offerings made to smoke on the altar (verse 5).

decisions.choice: But some sin offerings must not be eaten
decisions.reason: Readable states the rule first and then which offerings it covers.
